name: 39763-embedconcurrent-qwen3600m-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, `--gres=gpu:1`), sm90. Run on an otherwise idle node.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1 -- one engine, one GPU, and `--api-server-count` left at the engine default of 1 (a single API server process).
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=16, bounded at 20000 requests with a 900 s safety cap, first 10% warmup and last 10% cooldown by completion, leaving 16000 measured. The concurrency is part of the declaration and not a dial: a run at another value is a different setup, and it will complete without error.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets. Prompts exactly 500 tokens (min = max = 500), freshly sampled; `output_tokens: 1` is inert, an embedding request generates nothing. Sent to `/v1/embeddings`, which `spec.backend.request_format` pins, with `encoding_format: base64` and `embed_dtype: float16` on the body so the response carries a 768-wide float16 vector; the serve must be a pooling/embed serve or that endpoint does not exist.
purpose: A semantic search embedding service turning 500-token passages into compact vectors for 16 concurrent clients on one GPU.
launch:
# ENGINE: commit 0008729abfbd380d29e0a67a882c8f01220acd73 (v0.19.1rc0-260-g0008729abfbd).
# The interpreter and the hardware seal live in configs/env.yaml, which is this machine's and
# is NOT portable. Served over HTTP with `vllm serve`; host/port/served-model-name are not part
# of the declaration.
model: BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5

# LOAD-BEARING. `runner: pooling` is stated rather than left at `auto` so a run cannot quietly
# stand this checkpoint up as something else -- if it does, `/v1/embeddings` does not exist and
# the workload has nowhere to go. `convert` is deliberately NOT set: this checkpoint is natively
# an embedding model (`BertModel`), so the right resolution is `convert: none`, and forcing
# `embed` would wrap a converter around a model that does not need one.
runner: pooling

tensor-parallel-size: 1

# The three server numbers the workload is defined against: a 512-token window, 128 sequences,
# and a batched-token budget of 128 x 512, so a full batch of 512-token prompts is never split.
max-model-len: 512
max-num-seqs: 128
max-num-batched-tokens: 65536

# Per-request access logging is a fixed cost paid on the server's own request path, and it is
# off here so the number describes the serving work rather than the logging.
disable-uvicorn-access-log: true

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.80
